weather_line: Clearing in the hollows · bureaucratic pressure from the northwest

stories.headline: Subcommittee Dispatches Formal Mapping Party; Mapping Party Arrives at Marker 9; Mapping Party Cannot Find the Spur; Mapping Party Files Incident Report About This
body: A four-person Subcommittee on Unmapped Geographical Features mapping party — armed with theodolites, an eleven-digit reference number already printed on vellum, and a supervisor named Cresswell who had prepared remarks for the naming ceremony — departed the Ministry at half seven Thursday morning and reached the Harlan's Creek corridor by mid-morning. They did not find the spur. The gap in the treeline, witnesses confirm, was simply not where they were looking, which was slightly to the left of where it is.

Cresswell filed an incident report at twelve-oh-four describing the terrain as 'uncooperative' and the spur as 'apparently relocating between visits, which should be noted as a compliance issue.' A supplementary memo requested that Christine and Steve provide precise coordinates, a hand-drawn approach line, and a statutory declaration confirming the spur has not moved since Wednesday. Christine has received the memo. Christine has set it next to the sketch on the kitchen table, where it will remain until she decides otherwise.
The Room has not been informed of the mapping party's attempt. The Room is understood to be unbothered.

stories.headline: Three Accounts Reconciled Before Breakfast; a Fourth Attempts to Resist; Christine Gives It a Look; the Fourth Cooperates
body: Sources inside Gringotts confirm that four outstanding account discrepancies — some dating to a clerical error in the reign of the previous Vault Oversight Director, which the current Vault Oversight Director has been blaming on the previous one since spring — were resolved in full by Thursday morning. Three were settled before the chandeliers had been fully persuaded to wake. The fourth, a disputed interest calculation involving a compound rate that three goblin actuaries had approached and retreated from across two calendar years, was resolved after Christine sat down with it.

Griphook the Younger, reached for comment, said: 'The calculation was not incorrect. It was merely waiting for the correct approach.' He then returned to his ledger. No one pressed him further, as it was felt the situation had arrived at a satisfactory resting place and no one wished to disturb it.

stories.headline: Steve Notes That the Spur's Mouth Looks Different at Different Hours; Has Now Visited at Three of Them; the Jeep Forgives Him Nightly
body: It has come to the paper's attention that Steve has made three separate short drives to the corridor this week — early morning, midday, and once near dusk on Tuesday — not to run the spur again but simply to look at the mouth of it and confirm that it is still there and still behaves the way it did when they drove it. He has not told Christine this, though she has noticed the mileage and made no comment, which he understands to be permission.

The Jeep, for its part, has raised no objection to any of these drives. The enchantment that caused the engine to hold a low, aggrieved note on the return leg of any drive Steve conducted without adequate planning has been conspicuously silent all week. Observers note this is the longest recorded stretch of Jeep cooperation since the spring and attribute it to the quality of the line run Tuesday.

stories.headline: The Kitchen Table Holds Its Position; the Sketch, the Memo, and One Remaining Duck Consult Among Themselves; No Minutes Have Been Taken
body: As of Thursday evening the kitchen table bears the following: Ashworth's burnt-sienna sketch (the Room indicated by an unlabelled circle, no additions made since Wednesday), the Subcommittee's coordinate-request memo (unfolded, unread past the second paragraph), and the smallest of the three Jeep ducks, which migrated indoors for reasons Lucy has declined to explain and Ellie believes is simply where it lives now.
The arrangement has not been disturbed. Steve suggested at some point that the memo could go on the counter instead, and Christine observed that the counter is not where she put it. The table holds.

familiars_corner: Lucy: The memo from the Subcommittee was reviewed briefly on Thursday afternoon — Lucy read the second paragraph, appeared to find it satisfactory as a surface, and lay down on it. She has declined to confirm whether this constitutes a formal response.

Ellie: The small indoor duck was greeted with considerable warmth this morning. Ellie is fairly sure it is new but cannot rule out that it has always been there and she simply had not been looking in the right direction.

Jersey: A warm patch of sunlight moved across the kitchen floor at eleven-fourteen and Jersey followed it at a pace he considers brisk. The patch stopped near the table. Jersey considers the table's current situation to be fine and has settled nearby in a supervisory capacity.
founding_editor_note: That Cresswell fellow couldn't find a spur if it ran up his trouser leg. You want a proper survey? You use a level and you trust the ground. The ground always tells you. — D.

in_brief.sport: Thursday Lifting Report: the compound calculation at Gringotts has been informally estimated at the equivalent of a heavy deadlift; Christine declined to confirm the weight, which the sport desk takes as confirmation.
in_brief.forecast: Clearing by mid-morning in the corridor; the spur remains where it has always been; Subcommittee forecasts may vary.

storyline_updates.title: The Subcommittee's Jurisdiction Problem
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: The Subcommittee dispatched a four-person mapping party, led by a supervisor named Cresswell, who could not locate the spur. They filed an incident report describing the terrain as uncooperative and formally requested that Christine and Steve provide precise coordinates, an approach line, and a statutory declaration. Christine has received the memo and placed it on the kitchen table next to the sketch. She has not replied. Day 3 should escalate the Subcommittee's overreach further — perhaps Cresswell requests a second attempt with Christine present to 'guide' the party, or the Subcommittee votes to assign the Room a provisional eleven-digit number regardless of whether it has been located. Christine's patience may begin to have a shape that resembles a decision.
